albums.blurb: The Budos Band are a roughly ten-piece instrumental ensemble from Staten Island on Brooklyn's Daptone Records, the analog-soul label behind Sharon Jones & the Dap-Kings. Their second album, from 2007, tightens the debut's formula: Ethiopian-tinged Afrobeat grooves under heavy 1960s soul horns and fuzzed-out organ, with no vocals anywhere on the record. Several members later played in the backing band on Daptone labelmate Charles Bradley's records.
albums.reception: PopMatters rated the album 7 out of 10, concluding that in the Budos' familiar musical world "that which is most common yields the greatest pleasure."

albums.blurb: Lawrence is the New York soul-pop band fronted by siblings Clyde and Gracie Lawrence, an eight-piece built around horns, keys, and the two singers trading leads. Hotel TV is their third album, following Breakfast (2016) and Living Room (2018), and was released in July 2021 on Beautiful Mind Records, the label of pop producer Jon Bellion, who co-wrote and co-produced the record with the band.
albums.reception: Atwood Magazine's feature review described the album as "a cathartic, catchy, and emotionally charged collection of songs."

albums.blurb: Karen Dalton was a fixture of the early-1960s Greenwich Village folk scene, a twelve-string guitarist and banjo player whose weathered voice drew constant Billie Holiday comparisons; Bob Dylan wrote in Chronicles that she was his favorite singer there. Famously reluctant to record and unwilling to sing her own compositions, she made just two albums of interpretations. In My Own Time, her second and last, was produced by bassist Harvey Brooks in 1971 and ranges from Dino Valenti's "Something on Your Mind" to a stark reading of "When a Man Loves a Woman."
albums.reception: Largely ignored on release, the album was rehabilitated by Light in the Attic's 2006 reissue, which Pitchfork scored 9.0; AllMusic's retrospective review rates it 4.5 stars and calls it a more polished effort than her debut.
